name: ContentCortex – Outdated Content Alerts
author: Selvakumar Duraipandian

sections.description:
ContentCortex – Outdated Content Alerts helps editorial and content teams find published posts, pages, and custom post types that have not been updated within a defined cadence (e.g., 90 days, 180 days, or a custom duration).

Features include:
* Per-Post-Type Day Limits: Configure independent freshness targets for Posts, Pages, and any registered public custom post type.
* Outdated Content Report Table: Filter by post type and author, search by title, and sort by staleness.
* Mark as Reviewed: Reset the outdated clock for an article without updating post_modified_gmt or triggering sitemap/SEO changes.
* Exclusions: Exclude specific articles or entire categories/tags from ever appearing in reports.
* Automated Email Digests: Send weekly, monthly, or quarterly HTML summaries to team members with customizable branding, logos, and placeholders.
* Theme Overrides: Developers can completely customize email markup via theme templates ({theme}/contentcortex/email/digest.php).
* CSV Export: Export filtered content reports with built-in CSV formula injection protection.
* Dashboard Widget & Menu Badge: Instantly see how many items need review from your WordPress dashboard.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the contentcortex directory to your /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Outdated Content > Settings to configure enabled post types, day limits, and email digest schedules.
sections.faq:
Does “Mark as reviewed” modify my post modified date?

No. Marking an item as reviewed updates a private meta timestamp (_ocap_last_reviewed). It does not modify post_modified_gmt, ensuring sitemaps and search engine update signals remain clean.

How does the email digest schedule work?

Digests are scheduled via WordPress WP-Cron for your preferred day, time, and recurrence (weekly, monthly, or quarterly). For low-traffic sites, configuring a system-level cron job is recommended.

Can I customize the email template?

Yes! You can customize colors, headers, intros, footers, and logos directly in the admin settings with a real-time live preview. Additionally, developers can copy templates/email/digest.php to {theme}/contentcortex/email/digest.php to customize the HTML.
